members.label: Behringer
members.differences: Behringer's 2019 copy, in the Mk III's orange on black, with a full-size 37-note keyboard and all three of the original's filter versions to choose between. It adds MIDI, digital effects, a 32-step sequencer and an arpeggiator.

members.label: Mk I
members.differences: The first Odyssey, ARP's model 2800, made from 1972 to 1975: white-faced, with a 2-pole low-pass filter beside a non-resonant high-pass, two oscillators, sync and ring modulation, and a slider for every setting.

members.label: Mk II
members.differences: ARP's models 2810 to 2815, made from 1975 to 1978: black and gold, with CV and gate on every model and a four-pole low-pass filter close in design to Moog's.

members.label: Mk III
members.differences: ARP's models 2820 to 2823, from 1978 until ARP went bankrupt in 1981: orange on black in a redesigned case, with ARP's four-pole 4075 filter and an XLR output. Three pressure-sensitive pads (PPC) bend the pitch up and down and add vibrato, in place of the rotary pitch bend.
